item.text: {"inspirations":[{"title":"Exact symmetry quotient below the clean 35-parameter incumbent","hypothesis":"The clean 35-parameter model may contain another exact continuous or discrete reparameterization symmetry—within its query, SwiGLU, normalization, or adjacent projections—that permits at least one learned scalar to be removed without changing logits and without storing its value in a fixed buffer.","instructions":"Copy the attempt-clean-35p workspace. Symbolically enumerate scale, sign, permutation, and paired-matrix gauge transformations in the forward equations, using attempt-seed-36p to distinguish the already-removed global-amplitude gauge. For each candidate symmetry, impose a canonical constraint such as unit norm, fixed sign, or one analytically solved coordinate; delete the redundant Parameter rather than copying its fitted value anywhere. Retrain or fine-tune the constrained model, then verify parameter metadata, raw numel, unique storage, full autoregressive accuracy, and argmax agreement. Audit every buffer and literal introduced by the reparameterization, rejecting any candidate whose removed learned value reappears as a checkpoint-derived constant. Promote only a fully verified model with a clean trained-category review.","risk":"There may be no further exact redundancy, or the apparent symmetry may be broken by normalization, nonlinearities, biases, or decoding margins. A canonical constraint derived from the incumbent's numerical values could also be judged disguised calibration unless it follows analytically from the architecture.","parent_attempt_id":"attempt-clean-35p","reference_attempt_ids":["attempt-seed-36p","attempt-clean-35p"]},{"title":"Native constrained retraining of the 34-parameter query architecture","hypothesis":"The two query entries observed near or at -1 in attempt-raw-34p may represent a legitimate parameter-free sign convention rather than task-specific learned information; if that convention is specified independently and models trained from fresh random initializations reliably learn the task, a clean 34-parameter trained transformer may be possible.","instructions":"Copy the attempt-raw-34p workspace, but do not accept its calibrated fixed query buffers as evidence of category integrity. Re-express the two -1 entries through a simple architecture-level operation whose rule is chosen without consulting the parent checkpoint—for example, a fixed sign in the query construction or a tied antisymmetric basis—and remove the old checkpoint-derived buffers. Initialize every remaining learned scalar from scratch and train with the ordinary next-token objective across multiple independent seeds; do not initialize from the 36- or 35-parameter solutions. Record the pre-training architecture, initialization seeds, learning curves, selected-checkpoint rule, and failures as well as successes. Run the full verifier and a literal/buffer audit, and compare against attempt-clean-35p. Promote only if the fixed rule is demonstrably independent of fitted values, training materially changes learned weights, and manual category review is clean; otherwise retain the experiment solely as evidence that the 34-parameter route is not category-safe.","risk":"Because the -1 values were originally selected from learned query weights, changing their presentation alone does not resolve the review flag. Fresh training may fail, may depend on favorable initialization or checkpoint selection, or reviewers may still regard the sign convention as calibrated task knowledge.","parent_attempt_id":"attempt-raw-34p","reference_attempt_ids":["attempt-raw-34p","attempt-clean-35p","attempt-seed-36p"]}]}
